column1: Post-de-minimis landed cost scenarios — gua sha set

THE CHANGE: the $800 de minimis exemption is gone. CBP interim final rules of 24 June 2026 indefinitely suspended it for all modes of importation; the Court of International Trade upheld the rescission in Aug 2026; statutory repeal is set for 1 July 2027. Every commercial parcel now needs a formal customs entry with a 10-digit HTS code and full duty, regardless of value or carrier.
Sources: KPMG taxnewsflash 2026-06; BDO; Thompson Hine SmarTrade 2026-06; cbp.gov newsroom

WHAT IS NOT KNOWN: the HTS line for a stainless-steel facial massage tool set, and therefore the actual duty rate. Secondary sources cite ~37.5% above MFN for China-origin consumer goods (12.5% forced-labour tier + 25% Section 301) but that is NOT from CBP and must be confirmed by a customs broker. The per-entry brokerage/processing fee is also unknown and varies by carrier and service level.

THE STRUCTURAL ALTERNATIVE

Duty paid ONCE on a bulk inbound, then fulfil from a US warehouse. Per-parcel duty disappears; delivery drops from 8-17 days to 2-4; the US warehouse becomes a return address. CJdropshipping private inventory does this at 10 pcs/variant and 100 pcs total — far below Birstone's 200/200/500.

column1: THE HONEST CONCLUSION: $2,000 buys a market TEST on slow China-direct shipping, not a launch of a fast branded store. At roughly $4,000-5,000 the bulk-import + US-3PL structure becomes affordable and wins on every axis: 2-5 day delivery, duty paid once, full branding, local returns.
